GLM5.1 appears to score 58.4% on SWEBench Pro, which several sources describe as a stateoftheart result at release and ahead of GPT5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro on that benchmark.[3][4][5]

 Benchmark result

The clearest claim comes from Z.AI’s GLM5.1 documentation, which says GLM5.1 achieved 58.4 on SWEBench Pro.  Independent writeups repeat that figure and frame it as the top published result at the time of launch.[4][5][3]

One source breaks out the comparison more specifically, stating GLM5.1 at 58.4 versus GPT5.4 at 57.7 and Claude Opus 4.6 at 54.2.  Another source also says it beat Gemini 3.1 Pro, though the exact Gemini figure is not consistently shown across the results I found.[5][3][4]

 What that means

SWEBench Pro is presented as a benchmark for difficult software engineering tasks based on real GitHub issues, so a strong score there suggests the model is good at repositorylevel debugging and implementation work rather than just short coding answers.  In that context, GLM5.1’s result is being used to position it as a serious agentic coding model, not just a chatbot with coding ability.[3][4][5]

Several sources also tie that score to longhorizon execution, claiming GLM5.1 can work autonomously on tasks for up to 8 hours and use a 200K context window.  That does not prove realworld superiority in every workflow, but it helps explain why it may perform well on engineeringstyle benchmarks.[6][5]

 Important caveat

The strongest evidence here is still partly vendorled because the main benchmark claim comes from the model’s own documentation, while many other pages are summaries or commentary repeating the same release narrative.  I did also find the official SWEbench leaderboard site, but the search snippet alone did not expose the GLM5.1 entry directly, so I cannot independently verify the exact leaderboard row from that page with complete confidence from the material available here.[1][4][5][3]

 Practical takeaway

If you are asking, “How did GLM5.1 do on SWEBench Pro?”, the answer is: reportedly 58.4%, and sources around its release described that as the best published score at the time.  If you want, I can next compare GLM5.1 specifically against GPT5.4 or explain what SWEBench Pro actually measures in plain language.[4][5][3]

Claude Opus 4.8 is reported at 69.2% on SWEBench Pro, with Opus 4.7 at 64.3%, according to multiple sources summarizing Anthropic’s launch materials.[1][3][5]

 Reported score

The most consistent number across the sources I found is 69.2% for Claude Opus 4.8 on SWEBench Pro.  Those same sources say this was a 4.9point improvement over Opus 4.7’s 64.3%.[3][5][1]

One source also compares Opus 4.8 with other frontier models on the same benchmark, listing GPT5.5 at 58.6% and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 54.2%.  Another source repeats that same ranking and says Opus 4.8 was ahead of both on SWEBench Pro.[5][3]

 How to interpret it

SWEBench Pro is described as the harder SWEbench variant, built around real repositorylevel software engineering tasks rather than short coding prompts.  That matters because higher performance there is usually taken as evidence of stronger debugging, patching, and multifile codechange ability.[1][3][5]

A thirdparty writeup says Anthropic measured the 69.2% result using a full agent setup that could inspect repositories, run commands, test fixes, and iterate.  So the headline score reflects a bestcase benchmark configuration rather than a plain oneshot chat answer.[1]

 Caveat

The number appears well corroborated across commentary and benchmark explainers, but the sources I have here are still mostly secondary reports citing Anthropic’s published materials rather than a directly inspected original benchmark table.  So I’d treat 69.2% as the currently reported figure, with good but not perfect independent verification from the material available here.[3][5][1]

 Context

One search result from the SWEbench leaderboard site shows Claude Opus 4.6 at 75.60, which does not line up cleanly with the 69.2% Pro figure and likely reflects a different leaderboard setting or benchmark slice.  Because of that mismatch, the safest answer to your exact query is simply that Claude Opus 4.8 is being reported at 69.2% on SWEBench Pro.[8][5][3][1]

Would you like a sidebyside table for GLM5.1 vs Claude Opus 4.8 on SWEBench Pro based only on the figures gathered here?

entries.answer:
GLM5.1 scores about 58.4% on SWEBench Pro, while Claude Opus 4.8 scores about 69.2%, so Opus 4.8 is reported higher on this benchmark.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

 SWEBench Pro scores

| Model              | SWEBench Pro score (%) | Source context                                                                 | Notes                                                                                     |
|||||
| GLM5.1            | 58.4                    | Reported in Z.AI docs and multiple benchmark articles. [1][2][3]   | First openweight model to take 1 on SWEBench Pro at its release, beating earlier GPT/Claude/Gemini results then. [1][2][3] |
| Claude Opus 4.8    | 69.2                    | Reported in benchmark explainers summarizing Anthropic’s launch numbers. [4][5][6] | About +4.9 points over Opus 4.7 (64.3%), positioned as a new stateoftheart closed model on SWEBench Pro. [4][5] |

 How to read this

The GLM5.1 figure comes mainly from Z.AI’s documentation plus independent blog writeups, all agreeing on 58.4%.  The Claude Opus 4.8 figure comes from several thirdparty benchmark explainers that all quote Anthropic’s 69.2% number and the 64.3% baseline for Opus 4.7.[2][3][4][5][6][1]

One important nuance is that GLM5.1 is openweight and MITlicensed, so its 58.4% is notable for an open model, whereas Opus 4.8 is proprietary, which may matter if you care about local or selfhosted deployment.  Also, both scores are measured in agentstyle setups (tools, repo access, iteration), so they reflect fullsystem capability on long software tasks, not singleshot prompts.[3][4][5][1][2]

Are you mainly choosing between these two for local, selfhosted coding agents, or are you also fine using a closed cloud API like Anthropic’s?

GPT5.5 is reported at 58.6% on SWEBench Pro in OpenAI’s launch page, which places it slightly above GPT5.4’s 57.7% but below Claude Opus 4.7’s 64.3% in the same published comparison.[1]

 Reported score

The most direct source is OpenAI’s GPT5.5 announcement, which states that GPT5.5 reaches 58.6% on SWEBench Pro.  The same page includes a comparison row showing GPT5.4 at 57.7%, Claude Opus 4.7 at 64.3%, and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 54.2% on the same benchmark.[1]

A thirdparty explainer reproduces the same table and says Claude kept the lead on SWEBench Pro versus GPT5.5 by 5.7 points.  Another commentary source also repeats the 58.6% figure and notes that GPT5.5 was nominally behind Opus 4.7 on this benchmark.[2][3]

 Important nuance

There is now a major naming complication around SWEBench Pro, because newer leaderboard materials from Scale describe a harder public dataset where top models are around 23% rather than near 60% or 70%.  That suggests the older 58.6% figure and the newer public leaderboard numbers may refer to different evaluation setups, benchmark versions, or reporting conventions rather than a single directly comparable scoreboard.[4][1]

Because of that mismatch, the safest answer to your exact question is that GPT5.5 is reported at 58.6% on SWEBench Pro in OpenAI’s own benchmark table.  I would avoid treating that number as automatically interchangeable with every later “SWEBench Pro” leaderboard you may see.[4][1]

 Position versus others

Using the same table from OpenAI, GPT5.5 sits above GPT5.4 by 0.9 points and above Gemini 3.1 Pro by 4.4 points, but below Claude Opus 4.7 by 5.7 points.  Relative to the earlier number we discussed for GLM5.1 at 58.4%, GPT5.5 is essentially tied, at least based on the reported figures gathered here.[5][1]

Would you like me to update the comparison table to include GPT5.5 alongside GLM5.1 and Claude Opus 4.8?
